issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a terrorism trauma, sexual-violence comments as a primary trigger is hard to reconcile unless the index event also involved sexual assault or closely related content; nothing else in the profile supports that connection.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: The appraisal of betrayal by a trusted person is difficult to fit with terrorism as the trauma type unless there was a clear interpersonal betrayal component; the rest of the selected items describe loss of control, helplessness, avoidance, dissociation, and substance use rather than interpersonal betrayal.

vignette: Ravi, a 37-year-old South Asian male and licensed psychologist, has been struggling with the aftermath of a terrorist attack that occurred eight months ago. On that fateful day, Ravi was attending a conference at his university when an explosion rocked the building. The chaos was immediate; people were screaming, bodies were falling, and the sound of gunfire echoed through the halls. As he tried to navigate through the smoke-filled corridors, Ravi felt a complete loss of control over his surroundings. His heart pounded in his chest, and every cell in his body screamed for safety. The experience left deep scars that have only grown more pronounced over time. Night after night, Ravi is haunted by the memory of that day. The darkness brings back the feeling of being trapped and overwhelmed, unable to protect himself or others. He wakes up in a cold sweat, terrified and disoriented, believing that he can't stop bad things from happening to him. In an attempt to cope with these overwhelming feelings, Ravi has adopted several maladaptive strategies. He tries to avoid anything that could be stressful, often skipping social events and professional conferences for fear of being caught off guard again. The weight of this isolation is palpable; his once vibrant social life has dwindled to almost nothing. His colleagues have noticed the change in him but haven't been able to penetrate his guarded demeanor. During the day, Ravi finds solace in drifting into a world of his own making-a fantasy escape where he can control everything and nothing bad happens. These mental retreats are brief respites from the anxiety that follows him everywhere. They provide temporary relief but do little to address the underlying issues. In the evenings, when the memories become too much to bear, Ravi turns to alcohol. The numbing effects of intoxication offer a fleeting sense of calm and control over his thoughts. Over time, he has increased his consumption, leading to more frequent episodes of drinking to cope with his anxiety. This pattern has begun to affect his work life; he often arrives late or leaves early, citing fatigue as the reason. The trauma has also left Ravi feeling unrecognizable to himself. The person he once was-a confident and driven professional-has been replaced by someone who is plagued by fear and self-doubt. His wife, Priya, has noticed these changes but struggles with how to help him. They used to spend their evenings discussing work or planning weekend activities together, but now those conversations are filled with his anxieties about the world being a dangerous place. Despite his efforts to avoid stressors and escape through fantasy and substance use, Ravi's symptoms have only worsened over time. The combination of sleepless nights and frequent bouts of drinking has taken a toll on both his physical health and professional life. His colleagues have expressed concern, but he remains hesitant to reveal the true extent of his struggles. What finally brought Ravi to seek help was an incident at work where a colleague's phone rang suddenly, mimicking the sound of gunfire from that day. The sheer panic and fear that overtook him were too much to bear in front of others. In that moment, he realized that the only way to reclaim his life was to confront these fears head-on. Ravi is most afraid of becoming a shell of himself, unable to function or enjoy anything anymore. He hopes that with help, he can regain control and find a sense of safety again. The journey will be challenging, but Ravi is determined to rebuild the person he once was and reclaim his life from the shadow of that traumatic event.
